etymologies.heading: Etymology
etymologies.text: From 御(お) (o-, honorific prefix) + 代(か)わり (kawari, “compensation”).

etymologies.heading: Etymology
etymologies.text:
/arukohoru/ → /arukoːru/
Borrowed from Dutch alcohol, initially borrowed and pronounced as アルコホル (arukohoru) with evidence of a phonetic kanji spelling as 亜(あ)爾(る)箇(こ)保(ほ)児(る) (arukohoru). The medial /h/ appears to have fallen out due to historical kana orthography-induced spelling pronunciation (ho→wo→o), in the manner of the evolution of 凍(こほ)る (kōru). Compare French alcool, Italian alcol, Portuguese álcool, where Romance languages also lost the medial /h/.

etymologies.heading: Etymology
etymologies.text: From 久しい (hisashii, “long”, (of time)) + 振り (-buri, “first time after”).

etymologies.heading: Etymology
etymologies.text: Phrase composed of 仕方がない (shikata ga nai, literally “there is no way”).

etymologies.heading: Etymology
etymologies.text: Originally the 連用形 (ren'yōkei, “continuative or stem form”) of classical verb 借る (karu, “to borrow”), now also the 連用形 (ren'yōkei) of modern verb 借りる (kariru, “to borrow”).

etymologies.heading: Etymology
etymologies.text: Literary Chinese 分析 (fēnxī, “to separate, divide or split apart; to reason; to justify”)

etymologies.heading: Etymology
etymologies.text:
/ɕokipu/ → /ɕokiɸu/ → */ɕokiwu/ → /ɕokiu/ → /ɕokjuː/
From Middle Chinese compound 初級 /初级 (tsrhjo kjap?, literally “beginning + level, grade”). Compare modern Min Nan chho͘-kip or Cantonese co¹ kap¹.

etymologies.heading: Etymology
etymologies.text: Compound of 劇(げき) (geki, “drama”) + 場(じょう) (jō, “place”).

etymologies.heading: Etymology
etymologies.text:
From Old Japanese, from Proto-Japonic *inəti. Probably a compound of Old Japanese elements 息 (i, “breath”, i in compounds, iki on its own) + の (no, possessive particle) + 霊 (chi, “spirit, force, soul”).
Some analyses describe this as a compound using 生 (i, “life, breath”, i in compounds, iki on its own) as the initial semantic element. This is equally valid, as 息 (iki) and 生き (iki) are cognates.

etymologies.heading: Etymology
etymologies.text: From Old Japanese. Compound of 御 (mi-, honorific prefix) + 言 (koto, “word”). The mi prefix is generally limited to extremely high-status contexts such as gods or emperors.

etymologies.heading: Etymology
etymologies.text: From Old Japanese. Originally a compound of 御 (mi-, honorific prefix) + 事 (koto, “abstract thing”, as opposed to 物, mono, “concrete thing”).

etymologies.heading: Etymology
etymologies.text: From Middle Chinese 命 (mjængᴴ, “command”). Compare modern Mandarin 命 (mìng, “life, destiny, instruction”).

etymologies.heading: Etymology
etymologies.text: Potential form of 売(う)る (uru, “to sell”).

etymologies.heading: Etymology
etymologies.text:
⟨nuno₁⟩ → */nunʷo/ → /nuno/
From Old Japanese, from Proto-Japonic *nono.

etymologies.heading: Etymology
etymologies.text:
From Middle Chinese 布 (MC puH).
;“Hawaii”
Short form of ateji (当(あ)て字(じ)) spelling 布哇.

etymologies.heading: Etymology
etymologies.text: From 弱(よわ) (yowa, root of 弱い (“weak”)) + める (-meru, “-en, -ify”).

etymologies.heading: Etymology
etymologies.text:
戸(と) (to, “door”) + 棚(たな) (tana, “shelf”).
The tana changes to dana as an instance of rendaku (連濁).

etymologies.heading: Etymology
etymologies.text: From Middle Chinese 敵 (MC dek). First cited in Japanese to the early 1200s.

etymologies.heading: Etymology
etymologies.text: The Heian Kyoto pitch accent of indicates that the first two morae of this word come from 片(かた) (kata, “one of a pair”, pitch accent ).

etymologies.heading: Etymology
etymologies.text: From Middle Chinese 方向 (MC pjang xjangH).

etymologies.heading: Etymology
etymologies.text: First attested in 1920s.

etymologies.heading: Etymology
etymologies.text: 最 (sai-, “most”) + 高 (kō, “high”).

etymologies.heading: Etymology
etymologies.text: 欠 is a daiyōji replacing 缺.

etymologies.heading: Etymology
etymologies.text: Appeared in 舎密開宗 (Seimi Kaisō) of 1837-1847.

etymologies.heading: Etymology
etymologies.text: Likely the same word as 斟(く)む (kumu, “to consider people's feelings”) and 酌(く)む (kumu, “to serve sake”).

etymologies.heading: Etymology
etymologies.text: Ultimately from Middle Chinese 相續 (sjangH zjowk, literally “successively, one after another + to succeed, to continue”). First attested in Japanese in 820.

etymologies.heading: Etymology
etymologies.text:
⟨mi₁zikasi⟩ → /mizikasi/ → /mid͡ʑikaɕi/ → /mid͡ʑikaki/ → /mid͡ʑikai/
From Old Japanese.
First attested in c. 759 CE, in the Man'yōshū.
Appears to be derived as a compound, but the constituent parts remain obscure. The stem みじか (mijika) is also found in compounds, and in the now-obsolete adjective forms 短(みじか)やか (mijikayaka) and 短(みじか)らか (mijikaraka), indicating that the か (ka) is not the adjectivizing suffix か (-ka) (as in 静(しず)か (shizuka)), but rather part of the root.

etymologies.heading: Etymology
etymologies.text: Shift from standard みじかい (mijikai).

etymologies.heading: Etymology
etymologies.text:
⟨so₁ra⟩ → */sʷora/ → /sora/
From Old Japanese, presumably from Proto-Japonic *sora.
Found in the Kojiki c. 712 CE.

etymologies.heading: Etymology
etymologies.text: Cognate with 殻 (kara, “shell”).

etymologies.heading: Etymology
etymologies.text:
From Middle Chinese 空 (MC khuwng|khuwngH).
The Buddhist senses are a translation of Sanskrit शून्यता (śūnyatā).

etymologies.heading: Etymology
etymologies.text:
Not attested until a text from the Muromachi period with the spelling ツブ (tsubu).
An earlier form 粒 (tsubi) exists, which might have been the predecessor to this word; both must have been ultimately derived from a source cognate to つぶら (tsubura, “the state of being round and small”, obsolete).

etymologies.heading: Etymology
etymologies.text:
From Old Japanese 粒 (tubi₂), itself attested since the Shin'yaku Kegonkyō Ongi Shiki of 794:
*
数其滴 古経為_二字_一滴音宅、訓都飛
The number of those kernels; in the old Buddhist sutras, the character 滴 (dī) meaning "kernel" is to be read something like tek^([sic]); the native Japanese reading for this word is tubi₂.
This word, along with 粒 (tsubu), must have been derived from a source cognate to つぶら (tsubura, “the state of being round and small”, obsolete).

etymologies.heading: Etymology
etymologies.text: First cited to a work from the late Muromachi period; this word is a variant of 粒 (tsubu).

etymologies.heading: Etymology
etymologies.text: From Middle Chinese 粒 (MC lip).

etymologies.heading: Etymology
etymologies.text: Cognate with 荒(あら)い (arai).

etymologies.heading: Etymology
etymologies.text: Middle Chinese 組織 (tsu^X tsyik, “to weave threads together; to form from smaller components”)

etymologies.text: From Old Japanese.

etymologies.heading: Etymology
etymologies.text: 見(み)る (miru, “to see, look”) + 上(あ)げる (ageru, “to raise”)

etymologies.heading: Etymology
etymologies.text: 連 is a daiyōji replacing 聯.

etymologies.heading: Etymology
etymologies.text:
From Old Japanese. Derived from older form 閉(と)づ (tozu) via regular historical processes in the shift to the 上一段活用 (kami ichidan katsuyō, “upper monograde conjugation”) pattern. Over time, the distinction between ぢ (dji) and じ (ji) was lost, leading to the modern spelling of とじる (tojiru).
Development
Natural progression from Old and Classical Japanese 上(かみ)二(に)段(だん)活(かつ)用(よう) (kami nidan katsuyō, “upper bigrade conjugation”) verbs ending in -u to modern Japanese 上(かみ)一(いち)段(だん)活(かつ)用(よう) (kami ichidan katsuyō, “upper monograde conjugation”) verbs ending in -iru. For the Old / Classical form, see the 閉づ entry.

etymologies.heading: Etymology
etymologies.text: Compound of 黄 (ki, “yellow”) + 色 (iro, “colour”).

etymologies.heading: Etymology
etymologies.text: From Middle Chinese 黄色 (ɦwɑŋ ʃɨk̚).
